comment: Overlook native Linux desktop app. Google access tokens are sent in Authorization: Bearer headers. Token exchange, refresh, and revocation secrets are form POST bodies over HTTPS, never URL query parameters. The native loopback URL carries a one-time authorization code and state, not an access or refresh token; responses use no-store and no-referrer. Overlook exposes no public API. Attached evidence is native source/regression evidence, not a web DAST scan. Evidence: source/test document for unreleased v1.5.5 assessment candidate; details and limits in attachment.
validation: Source review plus OAuth encoding/callback tests and credential logging regression passed; TAC to confirm native-app DAST coverage.

comment: Overlook native Linux desktop app. Remove account disables the shared Gmail client, drains in-flight work, revokes the Google grant over HTTPS, clears in-memory tokens, then deletes OS-keyring entries and local account data. Failed revocation or keyring deletion reports incomplete removal and retains retry information. On 2026-10-22 the owner completed a live sign-in/removal test: authenticated sync downloaded 93 messages; before removal one OAuth keyring item existed; afterward the Gmail account, its cached messages/sync state and all matching keyring items were absent. The completed guarded cleanup demonstrates the revocation path returned success; no independent revoked-token replay or HTTP trace was captured. Removal requires connectivity and affects the user’s grant across this Google project’s devices/scopes. Provider passwords are removed locally, not changed at their issuer. See live supplement and source/regression evidence.
validation: Live user-driven sign-in/removal and before/after profile/keyring metadata verified. Remote revocation success is inferred from the guarded application path; no independent token replay performed.

comment: Overlook native Linux desktop app. Overlook does not provide an account-password change/reset service or issue cross-device sessions. Google and the selected mail provider own password changes and their session policies. Updating a saved IMAP password changes the local credential, not the provider password. Rejected Google refresh credentials map to SignInRequired. App disconnect explicitly revokes the Google grant; no claim is made that Overlook controls Google’s other sessions. Evidence: source/test document for unreleased v1.5.5 assessment candidate; details and limits in attachment.

comment: Overlook native Linux desktop app. Overlook does not issue non-revocable stateless session tokens. Refresh tokens are stored in the keyring and explicitly revoked on disconnect. Returned ID tokens are not used to authorize local users or API requests. Evidence: source/test document for unreleased v1.5.5 assessment candidate; details and limits in attachment.

comment: Overlook native Linux desktop app. The browser-facing sensitive endpoint is the transient OAuth callback. PKCE S256 binds code exchange. There are no cookie-authenticated state-changing web endpoints. Untrusted mail cannot navigate or submit forms in the isolated renderer. Evidence: source/test document for unreleased v1.5.5 assessment candidate; details and limits in attachment.

comment: Overlook native Linux desktop app. Google sign-in uses Authorization Code with PKCE S256 in the external system browser and a loopback redirect. comment: Overlook native Linux desktop app. The redirect is constructed from the bound 127.0.0.1 ephemeral port and fixed /callback path; it is not accepted from untrusted input. Token exchange sends the same redirect URI and original PKCE verifier. There is no response-driven redirect destination. Evidence: source/test document for unreleased v1.5.5 assessment candidate; details and limits in attachment.

comment: Overlook native Linux desktop app. Off-device Google OAuth/API, update, autoconfiguration, and remote mail-resource requests enforce HTTPS. The native OAuth loopback callback is HTTP by the installed-app protocol; it is not an Internet service. No hosted Overlook TLS server exists for SSL Labs. TAC should assess the desktop client’s outbound TLS controls. Evidence: source/test document for unreleased v1.5.5 assessment candidate; details and limits in attachment.

comment: Overlook native Linux desktop app. Production mail and HTTPS clients use Rustls with public WebPKI trust roots and hostname verification. IMAP TLS completes its handshake before authentication and returns errors on certificate/protocol failures; no accept-invalid-certificate switch is implemented. The test suite’s synthetic certificate is trusted only in cfg(test) fixtures, never in the production client. Evidence: source/test document for unreleased v1.5.5 assessment candidate; details and limits in attachment.
validation: TLS-backed synthetic resource tests passed. Provider/public-CA validation is delegated to the patched Rustls/WebPKI libraries. No SSL Labs scan of a desktop client is asserted.

comment: Overlook native Linux desktop app. Cryptographic uses: PKCE SHA-256 with a freshly generated 48-byte random verifier and 24-byte state; TLS 1.2/1.3 via Rustls with its secure default suites and ephemeral handshake keys; SHA-256 release-file integrity checks; OS-managed encrypted credential storage. Overlook does not implement its own encrypted mail database or application MAC/IV/key-rotation scheme. TLS keys/nonces are library-managed; vault encryption/keys/unlock policy are OS keyring-managed. OAuth token lifetime is provider-managed. Evidence: source/test document for unreleased v1.5.5 assessment candidate; details and limits in attachment.
validation: PKCE RFC vector and SHA-256 known-vector tests passed. Patched crypto dependencies have zero known vulnerability advisories in the current RustSec scan; maintenance warnings are documented.

comment: Overlook native Linux desktop app. TLS setup/handshake errors stop the connection before credentials are sent; certificate/protocol failures propagate as rejected operations. Keyring read/write/decryption failures become VaultError and do not trigger plaintext fallback. Overlook exposes no decryption API or network endpoint that reveals padding errors. TLS record cryptography and vault error handling are delegated to the respective libraries/OS service. comment: Overlook native Linux desktop app. The only inbound HTTP query parser is the loopback OAuth callback. comment: Overlook native Linux desktop app. Overlook has no server-side redirect/forward endpoint. The loopback callback returns a fixed completion page. Mail documents cannot automatically navigate: href values are isolated for host hit-testing, scripts/forms/frames are removed or disabled, and external links require a user action to open in the system browser. Remote resource redirects are limited to five hops, HTTPS, public resolved IPs, allowed ports/types, and no embedded credentials; private targets and downgrade redirects are rejected. Evidence: source/test document for unreleased v1.5.5 assessment candidate; details and limits in attachment.
validation: Real Chromium consent/redirect test and anonymous resource-fetch tests passed. This is native control evidence; external destinations intentionally opened by users are outside the renderer.

comment: Overlook native Linux desktop app. The mail renderer’s host uses fixed CDP evaluation scripts for DOM preparation/measurement and input hit-testing. Untrusted HTML is passed as serde_json-serialized data to DOMParser, not concatenated as executable JavaScript. Scripts, forms, frames and event handlers are stripped, page script execution is disabled, and all external fetches are intercepted. No user-authored eval or executable template feature exists. Evidence: source/test document for unreleased v1.5.5 assessment candidate; details and limits in attachment.
validation: Real Chromium test confirmed injected scripts did not execute and unsafe elements were removed; adversarial document tests passed.

comment: Overlook native Linux desktop app. There is no server-side template engine accepting user expressions. Native UI renders text values; generated HTML escapes user-controlled headers, and untrusted message HTML goes through structural sanitization. The isolated browser receives HTML as JSON-serialized data rather than interpolated executable code. Fixed print-page scripting does not evaluate user content. Evidence: source/test document for unreleased v1.5.5 assessment candidate; details and limits in attachment.
validation: HTML formatting/adversarial document tests and real Chromium isolation test passed.

comment: Overlook native Linux desktop app. Overlook has no hosted SSRF endpoint, but untrusted email resource fetches are treated as an SSRF-equivalent risk to the local device. Chromium is network-isolated. Explicitly consented resources are fetched by a separate anonymous HTTPS client without auth/cookie/referrer or proxy inheritance. PublicResolver filters actual connection IPs (including redirects), rejecting loopback/private/link-local/metadata/documentation ranges. Limits cover ports, MIME types, size, timeout and redirect count. User-configured mail servers are a separate intentional connection path. Evidence: source/test document for unreleased v1.5.5 assessment candidate; details and limits in attachment.
validation: Actual TLS resource tests and real Chromium consent tests verified consent gating, no identifying headers, private-redirect denial, and safe redirect handling.

comment: Overlook native Linux desktop app. Overlook has no XPath engine, XML query interface, or DTD/external-entity resolver. The limited ISPDB autoconfiguration XML is scanned as text for fixed tag names over HTTPS; it does not evaluate XPath, expand DTDs, or fetch entities. Email HTML/SVG is handled by the isolated/sanitized rendering paths. Thus an XML/XPath injection endpoint is absent. Evidence: source/test document for unreleased v1.5.5 assessment candidate; details and limits in attachment.
validation: Source review; see the referenced code excerpts.

comment: Overlook native Linux desktop app. Received HTML is untrusted. Ammonia allowlists remove executable elements, event handlers, forms/frames and unsafe schemes; inline CSS is restricted. The isolated browser additionally disables page scripts and applies CSP, DOM filtering and network interception. User header text in generated pages is HTML-escaped. Ammonia was updated to 4.2.4 for the current CSS URL filtering advisory. Evidence: source/test document for unreleased v1.5.5 assessment candidate; details and limits in attachment.
validation: Adversarial HTML/CSS tests and real Chromium script-injection checks passed; current RustSec scan reports no known vulnerabilities.

comment: Overlook native Linux desktop app. SQLite queries use bound rusqlite parameters for account IDs, mail IDs, user text and search expressions. Dynamic SQL fragments are selected by application code rather than supplied as user SQL. Full-text search uses a bound MATCH value and bound account ID. No network-accessible database or SQL query API is exposed. Evidence: source/test document for unreleased v1.5.5 assessment candidate; details and limits in attachment.

comment: Overlook native Linux desktop app. Application subprocesses use Rust Command with separate arguments. comment: Overlook native Linux desktop app. There is no hosted upload directory or server-side execution path.
